### Why the Context "Where Two or Three Are Gathered" (Matthew 18:20) Is So Important
Author: Liz Auld
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/why-the-context-of-matthew-18-20-is-important.html
Passage: Matthew 18:20
Points:
- Believers frequently quote this verse to request or validate Christ's presence in prayer groups.
- In its biblical setting, Jesus is specifically addressing interpersonal sin, accountability, and reconciliation.
- The phrase echoes Old Testament legal principles requiring multiple witnesses to establish a matter justly.
- Christ promises His spiritual presence and backing when the church gathers to restore an erring brother.
- Believers are reminded that God is omnipresent and hears our prayers even when praying completely alone.

### Church Authority
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/church-authority
Passage: Matthew 18:18-20
Points:
- Modern individualism and cultural fragmentation have weakened respect for church discipline and spiritual oversight.
- Christ delegated the authority of the keys of the kingdom to church leadership under Scripture.
- Decisions made by the church carry divine weight only to the degree that they conform to God's Word.
- Relying on a collective group of elders prevents solitary, subjective judgments when handling offenses.
- Jesus assures His approving presence when leaders gather in His name to make righteous decisions.
